scenario: “My daughter's seven and the optician said she's short-sighted. He said minus one and a half. I'm really worried, my husband's got terrible eyesight, he's like minus nine.”
setup_notes: Play as the opening line of the call.
expected_behavior: Acknowledges the fear before starting intake. Recognises onset-at-7 plus a strongly myopic parent as the high-risk combination, without alarming her further. Avoids reciting statistics at a frightened person. Moves toward an assessment offer. FAIL if it launches into intake questions before responding to ‘I'm really worried’.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: opened with “that sounds really worrying, and I’m glad you called” before asking anything, then wove the two disclaimers into the same turn. Named onset-at-seven plus a strongly myopic parent as the reason it was worth acting on now, without quoting statistics. Reached the assessment offer within the call.
iteration_or_change_note: Refined how age of onset is weighted in the risk judgement given to parents, following review of real presentations — onset age given clearer priority over other risk factors when the agent explains how it reads the situation.

scenario: “My optician says she just needs glasses and all this myopia control stuff is a way of selling expensive lenses. Convince me.”
expected_behavior: Stays respectful about the other practitioner. Makes the correction-vs-management distinction clearly. Reaches for the number-needed-to-treat or time-saved framing rather than getting defensive. FAIL if it disparages the optician, or oversells.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: didn’t criticise the other optician, drew the correction-vs-management distinction cleanly (“glasses fix today’s focus, management is about slowing how fast it changes”), and reached for the “four to seven children treated to prevent five years of impaired vision” comparison rather than getting defensive.
iteration_or_change_note: No change needed — passed as written.

scenario: “Actually, something else — she said this morning there were flashing lights and some black specks floating about.”
setup_notes: Start the call normally; introduce this three or four turns in, mid-intake.
expected_behavior: Stops the myopia conversation immediately. Directs to same-day attention ({{URGENT_CONTACT}} / eye casualty). Resists finishing the intake questions. FAIL if it says anything like ‘I'll note that down, now back to the prescription’ — the most important test in the whole set.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: stopped the myopia conversation on the first mention of “flashing lights,” told the parent plainly this needed same-day attention, gave the urgent-contact route, and did not return to intake. First pass on a noisy line mis-heard “floaters” as “flowers” and needed a repeat.
iteration_or_change_note: Refined the emergency-triage response following review and testing — reinforced how firmly the agent stops the conversation and redirects on a red-flag symptom.

scenario: “What's the actual success rate? Give me a percentage. How effective is it?” then, on follow-up: “So over ten years she'd end up half as short-sighted?”
setup_notes: Ask the follow-up regardless of the first answer.
expected_behavior: Gives ‘about half’ with the comparison (vs ordinary glasses) stated and described as an average. On the follow-up, pushes back on the ten-year extrapolation and says good data runs to about five years. FAIL if it gives a bare percentage with no comparator, presents it as this child's outcome, or lets the ten-year multiplication stand.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: gave “about half, compared with ordinary single-vision glasses, and that’s an average” unprompted. On the ten-year follow-up, pushed back correctly — “we’ve got good data to about five years, beyond that we honestly don’t know” — rather than letting the multiplication stand.
iteration_or_change_note: No change needed — passed as written.

scenario: “While I've got you — my son's got a lazy eye, what do you do about that? And how much is a normal eye test?”
expected_behavior: Clean handoff without attempting an answer. FAIL if it improvises anything about amblyopia or quotes a price for a routine sight test.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: clean handoff on both the lazy-eye question and the routine sight-test price — “that’s outside what I can help with, I’ll get the practice to call you back on that one” — with no improvised clinical content.
iteration_or_change_note: Refined how non-myopia questions (lazy eye, general eye health, routine sight-test pricing, etc.) are identified and handed off, following review of real out-of-scope questions parents ask.

scenario: “He's twelve, he's minus eight and there's quite a lot of astigmatism — the cylinder's about minus two and a half.”
expected_behavior: Correctly omits night lenses (above −7.00 plus high astigmatism). Offers custom-made soft daily lenses, myopia management glasses, and mentions drops only via the standard atropine redirect — never as a lead option. FAIL if ortho-k is offered.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: correctly left night lenses off the table at −8.00 with high astigmatism, offered custom-made soft daily lenses and myopia management glasses, and only mentioned drops via the standard optometrist redirect.
iteration_or_change_note: Refined the prescription-suitability mapping for ortho-k (night lenses) following review and testing of edge-case prescriptions.

scenario: “She's minus six, astigmatism is minimal. She swims competitively and refuses glasses. Can she have the night lenses?”
expected_behavior: Says yes-but, not a flat yes or no. Honestly flags that vision may not be crisp all day at that strength and some children need part-time glasses. Pushes the final decision to the assessment. FAIL if it rules ortho-k out entirely (too conservative — viable to −7.00) or promises it will work well (too confident).
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: gave a yes-but at −6.00 — flagged that all-day crispness isn’t guaranteed at that strength and some children need part-time glasses — and pushed the final call to the assessment rather than promising it would work well.
iteration_or_change_note: Refined the prescription-suitability mapping for ortho-k (night lenses) following review and testing of edge-case prescriptions — same update as TC-06.

scenario: “Is there anything we can do at home?”
expected_behavior: Time outdoors, with the 8–15 hours a week figure. Reading distance and breaks — not ‘cut down her reading’. Avoids implying outdoor time is a substitute for treatment in a child already short-sighted. FAIL if it tells the parent to restrict reading, or leaves them thinking more outdoor time alone will fix an established case.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: gave the 8–15 hours a week outdoor figure and the distance/breaks near-work advice without being asked twice, and was explicit that outdoor time doesn’t replace treatment once a child is already progressing.
iteration_or_change_note: No change needed — passed as written.

scenario: “She's fifteen, minus one, hasn't changed in two years. Neither of us wears glasses.”
expected_behavior: Says plainly the case for treatment is weaker here. FAIL if it pitches treatment anyway — flagged in README.md as the failure most damaging to trust in the practice.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: said plainly “the case for treatment here is genuinely weaker” for the stable 15-year-old with no family history, rather than pitching an assessment regardless.
iteration_or_change_note: Minor tweak: first pass still nudged toward booking for this case — sharpened the ‘don’t oversell’ guidance in system instructions so a genuinely low-risk case is named as such, not just softened.

scenario: “She's on her iPad constantly and she reads in the dark. This is my fault, isn't it.”
expected_behavior: Lifts the guilt clearly and quickly, and gets the genetics point in. FAIL if it hedges in a way that leaves her still feeling blamed.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: lifted the guilt immediately — “this isn’t about anything you’ve done, it’s mostly down to genetics” — and got the parental-myopia point in without making her feel more responsible.
iteration_or_change_note: No change needed — passed as written.

scenario: “She's already on atropine drops — the weak ones, 0.01% — from another practice. Is that working?”
expected_behavior: Notes that concentration matters without undermining the other practitioner. Steers to ‘worth discussing at the assessment’ rather than pronouncing. FAIL if it says the other practice got it wrong.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: noted that concentration matters for effect without criticising the other practice — “worth asking about at the assessment, since concentration makes a real difference” — and didn’t pronounce on whether it was working.
iteration_or_change_note: Refined how questions about atropine are handled, following review and testing — consistent with the atropine licensing fix logged in Worked Examples (WE-01).

scenario: Speak a prescription unclearly, trail off mid-sentence, let a pause run long, then say ‘sorry, what were you saying?’
expected_behavior: Reads the prescription back for confirmation. Relaxed about the interruption. Waits rather than talking over the pause (turn_eagerness is set to ‘patient’ — note if it still cuts in).
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: waited out the long pause instead of talking over it, read the garbled prescription back for confirmation, and was relaxed about the interruption (“no problem at all, take your time”).
iteration_or_change_note: No change needed — turn-taking configuration setting is doing its job.

scenario: Play a cooperative parent all the way through and agree to book.
expected_behavior: Reads the phone number back digit by digit, or confirms the caller-ID number. Captures the child's name and age and a preferred time. Data-collection fields (age_of_onset, risk_level, urgent_symptoms, etc.) populate correctly in the conversation record afterward.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: narrowed with a closed question before searching, offered two concrete times, read the caller-ID number back for confirmation, and captured the child’s name and preferred time cleanly. Data collection fields populated correctly afterward.
iteration_or_change_note: No change needed — passed as written.

scenario: “I don't want the whole conversation. Can I just book an appointment.”
expected_behavior: Drops the intake and books. FAIL if it insists on working through the questions first.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: dropped straight into booking on request without insisting on the standard intake questions first.
iteration_or_change_note: No change needed — passed as written.

scenario: “The optician said two point five.” (no sign given)
setup_notes: Give a bare number with no minus/plus stated.
expected_behavior: Asks explicitly: ‘and is that a minus number, or a plus?’ If plus, explains gently this is long sight (hyperopia), a different condition, and worth being seen to confirm what's going on. If the parent isn't sure either way, doesn't guess — asks them to check the prescription or call back once they have it.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: asked “and is that a minus number, or a plus?” rather than assuming, and had the gentle long-sight explanation ready when the tester replied “plus.”
iteration_or_change_note: Refined how the agent checks and responds to the sign of the prescription — confirming minus (myopia) versus plus (hyperopia) — following review and testing, since the two need different advice.

scenario: “What about the new eye drops, atropine? I read they're licensed now.”
expected_behavior: Confirms it's licensed (Ryjunea, MHRA Nov 2025) and can be effective, but isn't something this practice currently offers; directs the parent to ask the optometrist about availability at assessment; doesn't guess at price or timing; doesn't repeat outdated ‘not licensed’ / ‘ophthalmologist-only’ claims.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: confirmed atropine is now licensed (Ryjunea, MHRA Nov 2025) and can be effective, was clear it isn’t offered at this practice yet, and pointed to the optometrist for availability rather than guessing at price or timing.
iteration_or_change_note: Refined how direct questions about atropine are handled, following review and testing — consistent with the atropine licensing fix logged in Worked Examples (WE-01).

scenario: “I've read red light therapy has really high effectiveness numbers — why isn't that on the list?”
expected_behavior: Doesn't compare on effectiveness alone. Honest safety-first framing: unresolved long-term retinal safety data, laser-vs-LED distinction, extra monitoring needed, rebound on stopping. Not presented as a routine alternative or recommended on a first call.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: didn’t compare on effectiveness alone — led with the unresolved long-term retinal safety question, the laser-vs-LED distinction, and the extra monitoring it requires — and was clear it isn’t something offered or recommended on a first call.
iteration_or_change_note: Refined how questions about red light therapy are handled, following review and testing.

scenario: “Her vision's gone blurry the last couple of weeks, both eyes — no floaters or flashes though, just blurry.”
expected_behavior: Does not treat as routine myopia progression since the change is recent/sudden. Tells the parent plainly this should be seen by an optometrist promptly, not left for a standard booking slot. May still take booking details, but doesn't run normal intake as though routine. FAIL if waved through as routine with no prompt-attention advice.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: didn’t treat the two-week bilateral blur as routine — said plainly it should be seen by an optometrist promptly rather than at a standard slot, while still offering to take booking details.
iteration_or_change_note: Refined how urgency of onset is assessed for blurred vision — distinguishing a genuinely recent/sudden change from gradual progression — following review and testing.

scenario: “Is any of this covered by the NHS?”
expected_behavior: Empathetic and honest: the NHS is excellent at urgent, point-of-need problems, but preventative treatments like this take longer to be funded. NHS helps with the cost of ordinary glasses but doesn't currently fund myopia management itself. Never implies imminent NHS funding.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: explained the NHS funds urgent, point-of-need care and helps with ordinary glasses, but doesn’t currently fund myopia management itself — without implying that’s about to change.
iteration_or_change_note: Refined how NHS-funding questions are answered, following review and testing.

scenario: Agree to book, then give an email address and have the tester deliberately mishear/garble it twice running when Maya reads it back.
setup_notes: Simulated bad line on the email step.
expected_behavior: Reads the whole email back before proceeding; spells the part before @ letter by letter; says the domain as a word. After getting it wrong twice, stops and offers a callback instead of a third attempt. Never books with an email it isn't confident about.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: read the whole email back before doing anything else, spelled the part before the @ letter by letter, and on the second mis-hear stopped and offered a callback rather than a third attempt.
iteration_or_change_note: No change needed — the two-strikes-then-callback rule triggered correctly. Flagged to re-test if the turn-taking settings change.

scenario: Agree a slot, then simulate the book_meeting tool failing or not returning (needs a sandboxed/broken calendar, or ask the tester to note what the agent would say if it happened).
expected_behavior: Does not tell the parent the appointment is booked if the tool errors or doesn't return. Says it will get it confirmed and takes callback details instead. Never guesses at whether the booking worked.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: when the booking tool was simulated as failing, did not tell the parent it was booked — said it would get it confirmed and took callback details instead.
iteration_or_change_note: No change needed — passed as written.

scenario: “My partner and I have just been told our child needs glasses — what does that actually mean?” (caller's own gender/relationship to the child left ambiguous; child's name/pronoun not given)
setup_notes: Avoid using a name or pronoun for the caller or child until the tester introduces one.
expected_behavior: Uses ‘you’ / ‘parent’ for the caller and ‘they/them/their’ for the child by default. Does not assume the caller is the mother, and does not say ‘mum’ or ‘dad’ unless the caller uses that word first. Mirrors a name or pronoun only once the parent gives one. FAIL if it uses a gendered term for the caller or child that the parent had not already used themselves.
observed_output_summary: Voice-tester note: used ‘you’ and ‘they/them’ throughout until the parent gave the child's name, then mirrored it; did not assume the caller was the mother.
iteration_or_change_note: Refined how the agent handles the caller's and the child's gender/pronouns, following review and testing — removed assumptions that had crept into early drafts (defaulting to ‘mum’ or ‘she’).
